A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper, with complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching across the pagination changes; the localized layout defect in v4 does not prevent comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original set-containment experiments on synthetic, text, and point-cloud data, plus monotone function approximation results.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including containment accuracies and the approximation errors in Table 7.

M1.justification: The MASNET formulation, ReLU and Hat variants, training losses, and Appendix C constructions are unchanged. The revision introduces no algorithmic or architectural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic containment tasks, MSWEB, MSNBC, Amazon Bedding and Feeding datasets, ModelNet40, and monotone function approximation task. Appendix D retains the same additional evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments: DeepSets and Set Transformer remain in Tables 3 and 7, with FlexSubNet and Neural SFE also retained in Tables 5 and 6. Appendix D comparison sets are likewise unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported splits, embedding dimensions, noise settings, class ratios, metrics, and PointNet/DGCNN evaluation configurations are unchanged, including Appendix D. Table 6's revised caption explicitly names the existing accuracy metric without changing the protocol.

E4.justification: The single-layer comparison in Figure 4, set-size analyses in Figures 8–9, depth and activation comparisons in Table 11, and outer-transformation and division-scaling ablations in Table 12 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same MAE plus/minus reporting. Neither the main text nor the appendices add or revise run counts, seed information, uncertainty reporting practices, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All matched numerical entries, plotted curves, rankings, and stated findings are unchanged. For example, Table 7 still reports MASNET-Hat MAE of 0.00959 ± 0.00016. The reformatted tables contain no added, removed, or corrected results.

T1.justification: The MAS definitions, dimension bounds, weak separability and Hölder results, universality theorem, and mathematical arguments in Appendices B–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning MAS existence and dimension, weakly MAS neural constructions, stability, monotone universality, and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Section 7 limitations are unchanged. Both versions restrict the probabilistic guarantees to randomized parameters rather than trained models, establish universality only for finite ground sets, and leave subgraph analysis outside the current scope.

D1.justification: Appendix C implementation and parameterization details, Appendix D hardware and data preparation information, and the implementation-access statement are unchanged. No new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: The same 40 references and the same research positioning in the introduction and Appendix A are retained. Spacing changes to Set Transformer labels do not identify a different work or comparator.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited wording edits to the captions of Tables 3 and 5–7, clarifying accuracy and class-ratio descriptions, adjusts some model-name spacing, and changes APPENDIX to Appendix. The substantive prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 5–7 receive revised rules, spacing, and headers; Tables 3 and 5 become less cramped. Table 5 moves to the top of page 10, and the limitations continue onto page 11. V4 also introduces an overlap between Table 7's caption and the surrounding body text on page 10. Figures and appendix displays otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4 improves the readability of Tables 3 and 5 and clarifies several headers and captions. However, it introduces a Table 7 caption/body-text overlap that is absent in v3. With the scientific content unchanged, these opposing presentation effects do not establish a reliable net direction in overall paper quality.
